text:
hannah: dropping a short thread on a "sunset arc" playbook i sketched for long-lived tech debt items. goal: predictable runway + low friction consumer migrations. doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/sunset-arc-playbook :spiral_notepad:
liam: nice framing. quick q: how do you decide between "rationalize" vs "sunset"?
mina: prefer deterministic gates. propose three outcomes after triage: stabilize (keep), strip (rationalize/refactor), or sunset (deprecate + migrate). each outcome gets a runway and a pair (owner, steward).
oz: what metrics signal a strip vs sunset?
hannah: my triage signals: 1) consumer churn and coupling score, 2) incident exposure (blast radius), 3) product dependency (revenue/ux impact), 4) maintenance cost. i combined into a simple index in the doc. example thresholds: index < 3 -> sunset, 3-6 -> strip, >6 -> stabilize.
liam: can you paste an example manifest for a service we might sunset?
hannah: pasted small manifest example:
```
service: legacy-asset-ingest
owner: security-team
steward: platform-rt
status: candidates.sunset
runway: 90d
migrations: [cdn-migration, ingest-v2]
compatibility_shim: enabled
sunset_deadline: 2025-11-01
migration_quota: 5 consumers/week
observability: ledger_migration_missing, consumer_backcompat_fail
```
mina: we should attach a per-consumer migration quota and automated reminders. infra-bot can post owners weekly with outstanding consumers.
oz: compatibility_shim: what shape? small facade that translates old contract to new and emits `X-Migration-Pulse` header so we can measure who still calls legacy. shim also emits a `shim_warnings` metric when translation is lossy.
liam: for high-risk strips (eg model-serving/proxy), recommend a two-phased strip: (a) interface fence + request validation, (b) internal refactor behind fence with canary and fallback. keep read-only read paths stable.
hannah: agreed. added a canary recipe in the doc: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% ramp over 48h with rollback triggers: error spike > 0.2% OR p99 latency > baseline + 25% OR consumer_backcompat_fail > 0.05%.
mina: funding model? we need predictable capacity on squads. propose "paydown credits": teams earn 1 credit per sprint to spend on debt tasks; bigger slices get matched credits from platform budget. also do a quarterly 4-week "amnesty" sprint where teams can claim additional credits for top runway items.
oz: sounds political but workable. add a visible ledger in Console showing credits spent and runway progress per service.
liam: testing: mandatory compatibility harness that runs consumer smoke on feature-flagged route in CI. also a live synthetic test runner that exercises migration scenarios nightly and reports diff in outputs.
hannah: migration enforcement: if a consumer misses quotas for >2 weeks, infra-bot auto-tags the owning manager and schedules a migration retro. we should avoid hard kills unless agreed.
mina: rollback policy: if consumer_backcompat_fail > 0.1% for more than 30m we rollback canary, and open a P0 if > 0.5% for 15m. add those thresholds to the service manifest.
oz: add an escape hatch operator command that toggles global fallback to legacy for critical tenants and logs a `fallback-incident` event.
infra-bot: runbook created: #runbooks/sunset-arc/1810012345 with checklist and canary playbook. feature-flag `sunset_arc_mode` created (off by default).
hannah: next steps: i will convert this thread into an RFC draft, include the manifests, canary recipes, and paydown credit proposal. target: RFC by Friday, review at next arch sync.
liam: please include a migration dashboard mock with the three core KPIs: cross-service incidents, deploy-flakiness, and consumer-backcompat-rate.
mina: adding a note: ensure the manifest includes a probation window after runway ends — 30d soft-deprecation where shim is free but limited instrumentation; then hard-deprecation with audit.
hannah: thanks all. filing tickets and wiring dashboards now. :rocket:
infra-bot: reminder: architecture sync at 1810016000 (posted by infra-bot).
